# @saigontechnology/vision-camera-background-filter — full reference

> Real-time selfie background replacement for react-native-vision-camera 5.
> Concise index: ./llms.txt · Human docs: ./README.md
> This file is the complete contract for assistants. Every claim here is checked against
> the source in the same package; prefer it over inferring the API from call sites.

## What this package does

Three capabilities, probed independently because a device can have one without another:

1. **Live preview** — a background composited into the camera preview in realtime,
   entirely natively. No per-frame JS work; no segmentation mask crosses the bridge.
2. **Record-time capture** — encodes the composited frames as they are previewed, then
   remuxes the camera recorder's audio onto the result. The delivered file already has
   the background.
3. **Offline bake** — composites into an already-recorded file. The fallback for devices
   that cannot capture, encoders that fail mid-take, and gallery imports.

Native stack: iOS `VNGeneratePersonSegmentationRequest` + CoreImage `CIBlendWithMask` →
`CAMetalLayer`; Android MLKit `segmentation-selfie` (bundled) + GLES2 shader.

The package ships **ids, never copy**. No i18n, no theme, no navigation, no logging, no
state library. Everything user-visible crosses the API boundary as an argument.

## Compatibility

| | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| React Native | >=0.78, New Architecture ON (Nitro requires it) |
| React | >=19 |
| iOS | builds at 13; **segmentation requires 15+**, gated at runtime |
| Android | minSdk 24, compileSdk 36, Kotlin |
| Expo | SDK 53+, **dev build only — never Expo Go** |

Required peers: `react-native-vision-camera` >=5.1, `react-native-vision-camera-worklets`
>=5.1, `react-native-nitro-modules` >=0.36, `react-native-nitro-image` >=0.15,
`react-native-worklets` >=0.10 (Software Mansion — NOT `react-native-worklets-core`).

Optional peers: `expo-file-system` >=19 (for `/adapters/expo`), `expo-camera` >=17 (for
`/surfaces/expo-camera`).

No `@shopify/react-native-skia`. The live composite is native precisely so it can share
one rasterizer per platform with the offline bake — which also keeps Skia's 25 MB/ABI
`librnskia.so` out of the app.

## Installation — Expo

```bash
npx expo install @saigontechnology/vision-camera-background-filter \
  react-native-vision-camera react-native-vision-camera-worklets \
  react-native-nitro-modules react-native-nitro-image react-native-worklets
npx expo install expo-file-system expo-camera
```

`babel.config.js` — the worklets plugin must be LAST:

```js
module.exports = function (api) {
  api.cache(true);
  return {
    presets: ['babel-preset-expo'],
    plugins: ['react-native-worklets/plugin'],
  };
};
```

`app.config.ts` — permissions and SDK levels. This package ships NO config plugin, on
purpose: `expo-camera`'s plugin is the single source of all three permission strings, and
duplicating them produces conflicting Info.plist keys.

```ts
plugins: [
  [
    'expo-camera',
    {
      cameraPermission: 'Allow $(PRODUCT_NAME) to use your camera to record your video.',
      microphonePermission: 'Allow $(PRODUCT_NAME) to use your microphone to record audio.',
      recordAudioAndroid: true,
    },
  ],
  [
    'expo-build-properties',
    {
      android: { compileSdkVersion: 36, targetSdkVersion: 36, minSdkVersion: 24 },
      ios: { deploymentTarget: '15.1' },
    },
  ],
];
```

If NOT using `expo-camera`, write the keys yourself instead (never both):
`ios.infoPlist.NSCameraUsageDescription`, `ios.infoPlist.NSMicrophoneUsageDescription`,
`android.permissions: ['android.permission.CAMERA', 'android.permission.RECORD_AUDIO']`.

Then: `npx expo prebuild --clean && npx expo run:ios` (or `run:android`). `--clean`
matters on first install — autolinking discovers the module from its root podspec and
`android/build.gradle`, and a stale native folder will not pick it up.

## Installation — React Native (bare)

```bash
yarn add @saigontechnology/vision-camera-background-filter \
  react-native-vision-camera react-native-vision-camera-worklets \
  react-native-nitro-modules react-native-nitro-image react-native-worklets
cd ios && pod install && cd ..
```

- `babel.config.js`: `plugins: ['react-native-worklets/plugin']`, last.
- `android/build.gradle` → `ext { minSdkVersion = 24; compileSdkVersion = 36; targetSdkVersion = 36 }`
- `android/gradle.properties` → `newArchEnabled=true`
- `AndroidManifest.xml` → `CAMERA` + `RECORD_AUDIO` permissions
- `Info.plist` → `NSCameraUsageDescription` + `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription`

Autolinking needs nothing registered by hand.

### Monorepo (Yarn workspaces)

```js
// metro.config.js
config.watchFolders = [path.resolve(__dirname, 'packages')];
config.resolver.nodeModulesPaths = [path.resolve(__dirname, 'node_modules')];
config.resolver.extraNodeModules = {
  react: path.resolve(__dirname, 'node_modules/react'),
  'react-native': path.resolve(__dirname, 'node_modules/react-native'),
};
```

Jest needs the subpaths mapped by hand (it does not read `exports` the way Metro does):

```js
moduleNameMapper: {
  '^@saigontechnology/vision-camera-background-filter$':
    '<rootDir>/packages/vision-camera-background-filter/src/index.ts',
  '^@saigontechnology/vision-camera-background-filter/surfaces/expo-camera$':
    '<rootDir>/packages/vision-camera-background-filter/src/surfaces/ExpoCameraSurface',
  '^@saigontechnology/vision-camera-background-filter/(.*)$':
    '<rootDir>/packages/vision-camera-background-filter/src/$1',
},
transformIgnorePatterns: [
  // add: react-native-vision-camera|react-native-vision-camera-worklets|
  //      react-native-nitro-modules|react-native-nitro-image
],
```

Under Jest, mock `react-native-nitro-modules` (`hasHybridObject: () => false`) and
`react-native-vision-camera` — VisionCamera creates HybridObjects at module load, so
merely importing the barrel throws otherwise. With that mock the native probes report
unsupported, which makes the "device cannot segment" branch the default in tests.

## Verify before writing UI

```ts
import {
  getSegmentationSupport,
  isOfflineBakeSupported,
} from '@saigontechnology/vision-camera-background-filter';

getSegmentationSupport(); // { supported: true } when native is linked
isOfflineBakeSupported(); // true
```

`{ supported: false, reason: 'no-model' }` on a device that should work almost always
means the native module did not link. Rebuild; do not debug the JS.

## Host capabilities (dependency injection)

The record-time capture needs a scratch directory and a way to delete temp files. The
package will not choose a filesystem library, so they cross as two functions.

```ts
interface BackgroundFilterFileSystem {
  cacheDirectory: string | null; // PLAIN path, trailing slash, NO file:// scheme
  deleteFile: (path: string) => void; // best-effort; must not throw or reject
}

interface BackgroundFilterHost {
  fileSystem: BackgroundFilterFileSystem;
  onWarn: (message: string, error?: unknown) => void;
}
```

```ts
// Expo
configureBackgroundFilterHost(createExpoBackgroundFilterHost());

// Bare / custom
configureBackgroundFilterHost({
  fileSystem: {
    cacheDirectory: `${RNFS.CachesDirectoryPath}/`,
    deleteFile: (p) => void RNFS.unlink(p).catch(() => {}),
  },
  onWarn: (message, error) => log.warn(message, error),
});
```

- Call it once at startup, before any camera screen mounts.
- Calls **merge** field by field, so `fileSystem` and `onWarn` can be wired from separate
  places without one clobbering the other.
- Per-mount override: the `host` prop on a camera surface. Pass a **stable reference** —
  it is a memo dependency.
- **Unconfigured is safe**: no cache directory → capture skipped → raw recording handed on
  with `hasBackground: false` → your offline bake puts the background in. Slower, same
  clip.
- **Always wire `onWarn`.** Without it, a capture that failed and fell back is
  indistinguishable from a device that never supported one.
- `cacheDirectory` must be a plain path. Android's `MediaMuxer` rejects a `file://` URI
  outright; the Expo adapter strips the scheme for you.

## The camera surface contract

```ts
interface CameraRecording {
  uri: string;
  hasBackground: boolean; // describes the FILE, never the user's intent
}

interface CameraSurfaceHandle {
  record: (maxDurationSec: number) => Promise<CameraRecording | undefined>;
  stop: () => void; // safe when not recording and after the session is gone
}

interface CameraSurfaceProps {
  facing: 'front' | 'back';
  onReady: () => void;
  style?: StyleProp<ViewStyle>;
  backgroundId?: string; // undefined | 'none' = no filter
  backgrounds?: readonly BackgroundSource[]; // REPLACES the bundled defaults
  host?: Partial<BackgroundFilterHost>;
}
```

Two implementations:

- `VisionCameraSurface` (root export) — filtered, with record-time capture.
- `ExpoCameraSurface` (`/surfaces/expo-camera`) — unfiltered fallback. Accepts and ignores
  `backgroundId`/`backgrounds`, so the same props spread onto either.

`record()` semantics:

- **Resolves `CameraRecording`** — recording stopped normally (your `stop()` or
  `maxDurationSec`).
- **Resolves `undefined`** — the capture produced no usable file, e.g. the session was
  torn down. NOT an error.
- **Rejects** — a genuine capture failure. But on iOS, tearing down the session (the user
  navigating back mid-record) also rejects, so track an `unmounted` ref and stay silent in
  that case or you toast on whatever screen they landed on.

## Complete integration

```tsx
import { useRef, useState } from 'react';
import { StyleSheet, View, Button } from 'react-native';
import {
  BACKGROUND_NONE,
  DEFAULT_BACKGROUNDS,
  bakeFailureReason,
  findBackground,
  isBackgroundFilterAvailable,
  isCancelledBakeError,
  processVideoBackground,
  shouldBakeBackground,
  VisionCameraSurface,
  type BackgroundSource,
  type CameraSurfaceHandle,
} from '@saigontechnology/vision-camera-background-filter';
import { ExpoCameraSurface } from '@saigontechnology/vision-camera-background-filter/surfaces/expo-camera';

const MY_BACKGROUNDS: BackgroundSource[] = [
  ...DEFAULT_BACKGROUNDS,
  { id: 'home', source: require('./assets/home.jpg') },
];

export function RecordScreen() {
  const ref = useRef<CameraSurfaceHandle>(null);
  const unmounted = useRef(false);
  const [ready, setReady] = useState(false);
  const [facing, setFacing] = useState<'front' | 'back'>('front');
  const [backgroundId, setBackgroundId] = useState<string>(BACKGROUND_NONE);
  const [pct, setPct] = useState<number | null>(null);

  // ONCE per mount. Swapping mid-session tears down a live capture session.
  const [available] = useState(() => isBackgroundFilterAvailable({ backgrounds: MY_BACKGROUNDS }));
  const Surface = available ? VisionCameraSurface : ExpoCameraSurface;

  useEffect(
    () => () => {
      unmounted.current = true;
      ref.current?.stop(); // safe on a dead session
    },
    [],
  );

  const flip = () =>
    setFacing((f) => {
      const next = f === 'front' ? 'back' : 'front';
      // Both models are tuned for front-facing selfies.
      if (next === 'back') setBackgroundId(BACKGROUND_NONE);
      return next;
    });

  const start = async () => {
    try {
      const result = await ref.current?.record(30);
      if (unmounted.current || result == null) return; // torn down — not an error

      // Branch on the FILE, never on `backgroundId`.
      let uri = result.uri;
      if (!result.hasBackground && shouldBakeBackground({ background: backgroundId })) {
        const background = findBackground(MY_BACKGROUNDS, backgroundId);
        if (background != null) {
          const controller = new AbortController();
          setPct(0);
          try {
            const baked = await processVideoBackground({
              inputPath: uri, // trim FIRST if you trim at all
              background,
              fit: 'cover',
              mirror: false, // recorded files are never mirrored
              onProgress: (p) => setPct(Math.round(p * 100)),
              signal: controller.signal,
            });
            uri = baked.outputPath;
          } catch (e) {
            if (isCancelledBakeError(e)) return; // the user's decision, not a failure
            // A failed bake must ABORT the submit — uploading without the background
            // the user recorded with reads as data loss.
            throw new Error(COPY[bakeFailureReason(e)]);
          } finally {
            setPct(null);
          }
        }
      }
      await upload(uri);
    } catch (e) {
      if (unmounted.current) return; // the teardown we caused
      showError(e);
    }
  };

  return (
    <View style={StyleSheet.absoluteFill}>
      <Surface
        ref={ref}
        style={StyleSheet.absoluteFill}
        facing={facing}
        onReady={() => setReady(true)}
        backgroundId={backgroundId}
        backgrounds={MY_BACKGROUNDS}
      />
      {available && <BackgroundPicker value={backgroundId} onChange={setBackgroundId} />}
      <Button title="Record" disabled={!ready} onPress={start} />
      <Button title="Stop" onPress={() => ref.current?.stop()} />
      <Button title="Flip" onPress={flip} />
    </View>
  );
}

const COPY = {
  unsupported: 'This device cannot apply a background.',
  cancelled: 'Cancelled.',
  failed: 'Applying the background failed. Please try again.',
};
```

## Composing it yourself (without the surfaces)

```tsx
const videoOutput = useVideoOutput({
  enableAudio: true,
  fileType: Platform.OS === 'ios' ? 'mov' : 'mp4', // see pitfall #4
});

const { frameOutput, renderer, support } = useBackgroundFilter({
  effect: selectedId ? { kind: 'image', id: selectedId } : { kind: 'none' },
  backgrounds: MY_BACKGROUNDS,
  fit: 'cover',
  mirror: false, // NEVER mirror the background
  mirrorCamera: facing === 'front', // mirror the camera + mask together
});

<Camera
  isActive
  device={facing}
  outputs={frameOutput != null ? [videoOutput, frameOutput] : [videoOutput]}
  style={StyleSheet.absoluteFill}
  onStarted={onReady}
/>;
{
  /* Mount ONLY while filtering — with no frames it draws a blank rectangle over
     the live preview instead of the camera. */
}
renderer != null && <BackgroundRendererView style={StyleSheet.absoluteFill} renderer={renderer} />;
```

Record-time capture, manually:

```tsx
// 1. Start the camera's recorder FIRST and await it. Order matters for lip sync.
let started;
const finished = new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
  started = recorder.startRecording(resolve, reject);
  started.catch(reject);
});
await started;

// 2. Then start the composite encoder.
const capture = isCompositeCaptureSupported(renderer)
  ? startCompositeCapture({
      renderer,
      outputPath: `${cacheDir}composite-${Date.now()}.mp4`,
      maxOutputHeight: 1920,
      aspectRatio: 9 / 16, // match what the recorder writes
    })
  : null;

// 3. Stop BOTH at the same instant (from your stop handler).
recorder.stopRecording().catch(() => {});
capture?.stop().catch(() => {});

// 4. Join them. Neither track is re-encoded — ~1 s for a 30 s clip.
const rawPath = await finished;
const { outputPath, capturePath } = await capture.finish({ audioSourcePath: rawPath });
deleteFile(capturePath); // both inputs are consumed by the mux
deleteFile(rawPath);
```

## Full export list

### Capability

- `isBackgroundFilterAvailable(options?: { backgrounds? }): boolean` — assets ⋀ device
  support. **Contains no feature flag by design**; `&&` your own for a staged rollout.
- `getSegmentationSupport(): SegmentationSupport` — `{ supported, reason? }` where reason
  is `'os-version' | 'no-model' | 'unsupported-device'`.
- `useSegmentationSupport(): SegmentationSupport` — hook form.
- `isCompositeCaptureSupported(renderer): boolean`
- `isOfflineBakeSupported(): boolean`
- `shouldBakeBackground(opts): boolean` — pure. Opts: `background`, `alreadyComposited?`,
  `filterAvailable?`, `bakeSupported?`, `backgrounds?`. The last three are injectable so
  the decision is testable without a device.

### Surfaces

- `VisionCameraSurface`, `ExpoCameraSurface` (subpath), types `CameraSurfaceHandle`,
  `CameraRecording`, `CameraSurfaceProps`.

### Live preview

- `useBackgroundFilter(opts): { frameOutput, renderer, support }`
  - `effect: { kind: 'image', id } | { kind: 'blur', radius } | { kind: 'none' }` —
    **`blur` is plumbed through the type but NOT implemented**; it counts as inactive.
  - `backgrounds?` — replaces the defaults.
  - `fit?: 'cover' | 'contain'` (default `'cover'`)
  - `mirror?: boolean` (default false) — mirrors the BACKGROUND. Leave false.
  - `mirrorCamera?: boolean` (default false) — mirrors the camera + mask. Set true on the
    front camera so the filtered preview matches the unfiltered one.
  - `targetResolution?` (default `{ width: 960, height: 1280 }` — 4:3)
  - `previewSizedFrames?: boolean` (default false)
- `BackgroundRendererView` — `{ renderer, style }`.

### Record & bake

- `startCompositeCapture({ renderer, outputPath, maxOutputHeight?, aspectRatio? })`
  → `CompositeCapture { capturePath, stop(), finish({ audioSourcePath?, outputPath? }), cancel() }`
  - `stop()` is idempotent and returns the same path on repeat calls.
  - `cancel()` resolves the partial path (delete it) or `null` if nothing was written.
- `processVideoBackground({ inputPath, background, outputPath?, fit?, mirror?, maxOutputHeight?, onProgress?, signal? })`
  → `Promise<{ outputPath, durationMs }>`
  - `onProgress` is 0..1, throttled natively to ~10/s, called on the JS thread.
  - A cancelled or failed run deletes its own partial output.

### Backgrounds

- `DEFAULT_BACKGROUNDS` (`office`, `studio`, `library`), `DEFAULT_BACKGROUND_IDS`,
  `MAX_BACKGROUND_EDGE_PX` (1920)
- `BACKGROUND_NONE` (`'none'`), `isBackgroundSelected(id)`,
  `findBackground(list, id)` (generic in the element type — a widened
  `BackgroundSource` comes back widened), `hasBackgrounds(list)`
- `resolveBackgroundUri(background)`
- `BackgroundSource = { id: string; source: number | { uri: string } }`

### Errors

- `BackgroundFilterError` with `code: 'unsupported' | 'decode-failed' | 'encode-failed' | 'cancelled' | 'io'`
  — the only type the package rejects with. `isBackgroundFilterError(e)` guards it.
- `bakeFailureReason(e) → 'unsupported' | 'cancelled' | 'failed'` — map to your own copy.
  Anything unrecognised reports `'failed'`, so a future code cannot surface untranslated.
- `BakeCancelledError` + `isBakeCancelled(e)` — the sentinel you throw to unwind a submit
  pipeline after a user cancel.
- `isCancelledBakeError(e)` — checks the PACKAGE's error, BEFORE conversion to the
  sentinel. **Do not confuse these two.** Getting them backwards reclassifies every
  genuine encoder failure as "you cancelled", which swallows the failure entirely.

### Host

`configureBackgroundFilterHost`, `resolveBackgroundFilterHost`, `useBackgroundFilterHost`,
`resetBackgroundFilterHost` (test seam), `NULL_FILE_SYSTEM`, `optionalRequire`, types
`BackgroundFilterHost`, `BackgroundFilterFileSystem`.

### Geometry

`computeBackgroundLayout`, `fitScale`, `mirrorRectHorizontally`, `rotateSize`,
type `BackgroundLayout` — the single specification both native mirrors implement.

## Pitfalls, with causes

1. **Branching on the selected background instead of `result.hasBackground`.** A capture
   that failed falls back to the raw recording and reports `false` even though a
   background was picked. Branch on the selection and those clips upload unfiltered.
2. **Treating `record() === undefined` as an error.** It means the session was torn down.
   Only a rejection is a failure — and on iOS a teardown rejects too, so gate on an
   `unmounted` ref.
3. **Resolving the surface on every render.** Use `useState(() => …)`. Swapping surfaces
   mid-session tears down a live capture session.
4. **iOS clip has no audio.** `AVCaptureMovieFileOutput` writes a QuickTime container
   regardless of what you ask for, so `fileType: 'mp4'` produces a QuickTime file NAMED
   `.mp4`; `AVURLAsset` picks its parser from the extension and the mp4 parser silently
   DISCARDS the QuickTime-style audio sample entry. Use `'mov'` on iOS, `'mp4'` on
   Android (whose `MediaExtractor` sniffs content and whose muxer wants a real mp4).
5. **Audio ~370 ms ahead of video.** The composite encoder takes t=0 from its first frame.
   Start it before the recorder and the audio belongs to a moment the video does not have.
   Start the recorder first, `await` its promise, then start the capture — the audio is
   then LONGER at the head by exactly that gap, which `muxAudio` removes by comparing
   durations.
6. **Stopping the capture late.** Stop it at the same instant as the recorder, not when
   the recorder's file arrives. The remux infers the head offset from the duration
   difference; a loose tail corrupts that inference.
7. **`pixelFormat: 'native'`.** Resolves to whatever the session negotiated, which on
   Android can be a PRIVATE format with no CPU-accessible planes; a Galaxy S22 rejects it
   outright (`PRIVATE format with resolution 1280x720 is not supported for
   ImageAnalysis`). Use `'yuv'` — both renderers consume planar YUV directly.
8. **`try { require('expo-file-system') }` to make a dep optional.** Metro resolves
   `require` statically while building the module graph, so an uninstalled package is a
   BUILD error and the catch never runs. Optionality comes from the subpath exports only.
9. **Non-empty `react-native.config.js` platform entries.** Paths there resolve relative
   to the package root, so an absolute `sourceDir`/`podspecPath` gets re-joined onto that
   root, points nowhere, and the module vanishes from Android autolinking with NO error
   (iOS keeps working, so it looks Android-specific). Keep both entries `{}`.
10. **Oversized background images.** The native renderers downscale to 1920, but that does
    not protect a thumbnail rendered through your own image loader. An 8192x5464 source
    decodes to ~171 MB of RGBA → `RuntimeException: trying to draw too large bitmap` on
    Android. Ship them near 1080x1920.
11. **Mounting `BackgroundRendererView` when `renderer` is null.** It draws a blank
    rectangle over the live preview instead of the camera.
12. **Leaving `aspectRatio` at 0 on the capture.** The composited frames are shaped for
    the PREVIEW (4:3, matching the unfiltered field of view) while the recorder writes
    9:16, so a filtered clip comes out a different shape than an unfiltered one.
13. **Full 1080p frames.** Measured on a Galaxy S22: 960x1280 → 28.7 fps; 1440x1920 →
    22.2 fps, under the 24 fps budget on a flagship. iPhone 11 sits at 24.3–26.1 at
    1440x1920, i.e. no margin.
14. **`previewSizedFrames: true` while recording.** It caps the capture's resolution
    (540x960 measured on an S22), because the capture encodes those same frames.
15. **Expecting RN overlays in the file.** Teleprompters, countdowns and watermarks are
    outside both composites. Intentional.
16. **Baking a clip that already has a background.** `shouldBakeBackground` checks
    `alreadyComposited` first for this reason — segmenting a composited frame composites
    over the wrong subject, which looks far worse than not baking.
17. **Treating `CameraRecording.uri` as a `file://` URI on Android.** It is a PLAIN
    absolute path: VisionCamera's recorder returns `file.absolutePath`, and this
    package's composite/mux output is schemeless deliberately because `MediaMuxer`
    rejects a URI. media3/ExoPlayer routes a `null`-scheme `Uri` to `FileDataSource`, so
    the clip PLAYS — but `expo-video`'s `generateThumbnailsAsync` gates on
    `URLUtil.isFileUrl` (a literal `startsWith("file:")`), fails it, and hands the path
    to the NETWORK overload of `setDataSource`, which throws. Symptom: video plays,
    thumbnail strip is empty, Android only, so it looks like a thumbnail bug rather than
    a URI-scheme one. Fix at the point of use:
    `const toPlayerSource = (v) => (v.startsWith('/') ? 'file://' + v : v)` applied to
    the PLAYER SOURCE ONLY. Keep the plain path for `processVideoBackground`, trimmers,
    muxers and upload — prefixing globally breaks those instead.

## Performance budget

- Preview >=24 fps on iPhone 12 / Pixel 6 class. Measured ~30 fps on a Galaxy S22 at the
  default resolution.
- Bake: 0.3–1x realtime → 10–60 s for a 30 s clip. Needs progress UI and a cancel path.
  Cap `maxOutputHeight` to 720 on slow devices if it exceeds ~60 s.
- Remux: ~1 s for a 30 s clip (container operation, no re-encode).
- Native size: ~700 KB per ABI, plus MLKit's bundled model (~5 MB, ABI-independent).

## Architecture notes

VisionCamera 5 splits the session into independent parallel outputs. Compositing in a
`CameraFrameOutput` does NOT affect what `CameraVideoOutput` records, and
`FrameRenderer.renderFrame(frame: Frame)` accepts only a VisionCamera `Frame` — so a
composited image cannot be routed back into the `Recorder`. Hence the two paths above.

Parity between the live composite and the offline bake is structural, not tested-in:
`src/composite/geometry.ts` is the single specification for all fit/crop/mirror/rotation
math, each platform has exactly ONE native mirror of it (`BackgroundGeometry.kt` /
`.swift`) shared by that platform's live and offline paths, and `BackgroundGeometryTest.kt`
asserts the Kotlin mirror produces the same numbers as the TypeScript. Do not add a third
implementation.

Audio is never captured, encoded or timed by this package. The camera's own recorder owns
the microphone; the package takes its audio TRACK verbatim and puts it beside the
composited video. That is why the A/V sync class of bug does not apply here.
